from.place: The derived couple construction is functorial in the couple; iterating gives maps on all E_r and at infinity

title: Functoriality of derived exact couples
statement: Let $(D,E,\alpha,f,g)$ and $(D',E',\alpha',f',g')$ be exact couples [def-sp-exact-couple] in the same abelian category. Suppose maps $t_D:D\to D'$ and $t_E:E\to E'$ preserve bidegrees and satisfy $t_D\alpha=\alpha't_D$, $t_Df=f't_E$, and $t_Eg=g't_D$ (that is, they form a morphism of exact couples). Then the maps induced by $(t_D,t_E)$ on the derived couples are well defined and commute with the derived structure maps. Iterating the construction gives a morphism on every page $E_r$ commuting with $d_r$, and the induced map carries $Z_\infty$ into $Z'_\infty$ and $B_\infty$ into $B'_\infty$, hence induces a morphism $E_\infty\to E'_\infty$ as in [def-sp-convergence].

proof.text: Write $d=g\circ f$ and $d'=g'\circ f'$. The three commutative squares for a morphism of couples give $t_Ed=d't_E$. Hence $t_E$ carries $\ker d$ into $\ker d'$ and $\operatorname{im}d$ into $\operatorname{im}d'$, so the universal property of the kernel and quotient defines a map from the derived $E$-term of the first couple to the derived $E'$-term of the second. Likewise $t_D\alpha=\alpha't_D$ carries $\operatorname{im}\alpha$ into $\operatorname{im}\alpha'$, defining the map on the derived $D$-terms. The identities with $\alpha,f,g$ descend to the derived structure maps because the defining maps are restrictions, factorizations, and quotient maps; thus the induced pair is a morphism of derived couples.

proof.text: By the exactness assertion for the derived couple (item 3, and item 4 for the iteration), the preceding construction may be applied to every iterate of both couples: start with $C_2=C=(D,E,\alpha,f,g)$ and $\tilde C_2=(D',E',\alpha',f',g')$ and define $C_{r+1}$, $\tilde C_{r+1}$ as the derived couples of $C_r$, $\tilde C_r$ (couples of type $r-2$). Induction on $r$, applying the previous step to the type-$(r-2)$ couples $C_r$ and $\tilde C_r$, gives morphisms of couples $C_r\to\tilde C_r$ for all $r\ge2$, whose $D$-component is the restriction of $t_D$ to $D_r^{p,q}=\operatorname{im}(\alpha^{r-2})\subseteq D^{p,q}$. On the $E$-terms these are maps $\varphi_r:E_r\to\tilde E_r$ with $\varphi_2=t_E$; the equality $\varphi_r d_r=\tilde d_r\varphi_r$, where $d_r=g_r\circ f_r$ and $\tilde d_r=\tilde g_r\circ\tilde f_r$, follows from the commutation of the $r$-th morphism with $f_r$ and $g_r$. Thus every page map commutes with its differential.

The compatible page maps preserve cycles and boundaries in the recursive construction of [def-sp-convergence]. Inductively, $\varphi_2$ maps each $Z_r$ into $Z_r'$ and each $B_r$ into $B_r'$, and the induced map on $Z_r/B_r$ is $\varphi_r$; the induction step uses that $\varphi_r$ commutes with $d_r$. Passing to the intersection and union gives $\varphi_2(Z_\infty)\subseteq Z_\infty'$ and $\varphi_2(B_\infty)\subseteq B_\infty'$, so the quotient map $E_\infty=Z_\infty/B_\infty\to Z_\infty'/B_\infty'=E_\infty'$ is well defined.

lean.statement: theorem derivedCoupleFunctoriality (X Y : BigradedExactCouple C 0) (T : CoupleMorphism X Y) : (∃ M : ∀ n : ℕ, CoupleMorphism (X.pageCouple n) (Y.pageCouple n), (∀ p q : ℤ, (M 0).tD p q = T.tD p q) ∧ (∀ p q : ℤ, (M 0).tE p q = T.tE p q) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (p q : ℤ), (M (n + 1)).tD p q ≫ (Y.pageCouple n).derivedDInclusion p q = (X.pageCouple n).derivedDInclusion p q ≫ (M n).tD p q) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (p q : ℤ), ∃ k : kernel ((X.pageCouple n).d p q) ⟶ kernel ((Y.pageCouple n).d p q), k ≫ kernel.ι ((Y.pageCouple n).d p q) = kernel.ι ((X.pageCouple n).d p q) ≫ (M n).tE p q ∧ (X.pageCouple n).derivedEProjection p q ≫ (M (n + 1)).tE p q = k ≫ (Y.pageCouple n).derivedEProjection p q) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (p q : ℤ), (M n).tE p q ≫ (Y.pageCouple n).d p q = (X.pageCouple n).d p q ≫ (M n).tE (p + 2 + n) (q - 1 - n))) ∧ (∀ (LX : LimitSubobjects X) (LY : LimitSubobjects Y), (∀ p q : ℤ, (LY.Z p q).Factors ((LX.Z p q).arrow ≫ T.tE p q) ∧ (LY.B p q).Factors ((LX.B p q).arrow ≫ T.tE p q)) ∧ (∀ p q : ℤ, ∃ (e : X.pageInfinity LX p q ⟶ Y.pageInfinity LY p q) (z : (LX.Z p q : C) ⟶ (LY.Z p q : C)), (LX.Z p q).arrow ≫ T.tE p q = z ≫ (LY.Z p q).arrow ∧ z ≫ cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE (LY.B p q) (LY.Z p q) (limitBoundary_le_cycle Y LY p q)) = cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE (LX.B p q) (LX.Z p q) (limitBoundary_le_cycle X LX p q)) ≫ e) )
